act.name: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
act.source_authority: Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India
act.description: Central code governing civil-court jurisdiction, suits, decrees, execution, appeals and settlement procedure.

sections.title: Courts to try all civil suits unless barred.
sections.text: Section 9 recognizes civil-court jurisdiction over suits of a civil nature unless cognizance is barred.
sections.plain_language_summary: Civil courts can ordinarily hear civil disputes unless a law expressly or impliedly excludes them.

sections.title: Stay of suit.
sections.text: Section 10 governs stay of a later suit where the matter in issue is directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit.
sections.plain_language_summary: A later civil suit may be paused when the same substantial dispute is already pending between the relevant parties.

sections.title: Res judicata.
sections.text: Section 11 prevents re-litigation of a matter directly and substantially decided in a qualifying former suit.
sections.plain_language_summary: A dispute already finally decided between the relevant parties generally cannot be tried again.

sections.title: Other suits to be instituted where defendants reside or cause of action arises.
sections.text: Section 20 provides territorial rules for instituting other suits based on the defendant's residence or the cause of action.
sections.plain_language_summary: Many civil suits are filed where the defendant resides or where the cause of action arose.

sections.title: Notice.
sections.text: Section 80 governs notice before instituting specified suits against the Government or public officers.
sections.plain_language_summary: A statutory notice is generally required before certain civil suits against Government or a public officer.

sections.title: Settlement of disputes outside the Court.
sections.text: Section 89 provides for referral to specified methods of settlement outside court where appropriate.
sections.plain_language_summary: A civil court may refer suitable disputes to arbitration, conciliation, judicial settlement, Lok Adalat or mediation.

sections.title: Appeal from original decree.
sections.text: Section 96 governs appeals from original decrees subject to the Code.
sections.plain_language_summary: A qualifying original civil decree may be appealed under the statutory rules.

sections.title: Saving of inherent powers of Court.
sections.text: Section 151 preserves the court's inherent powers to make orders necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of process.
sections.plain_language_summary: Civil courts retain inherent power to protect justice and prevent misuse of court procedure.
